chunks: From him, from Abu al-Nasr Ismail ibn Abdullah ibn Maimoon ibn al-Hamid ibn Abi al-Rijal al-Ajli, who said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Saad al-Kahili narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Bashir ibn Ghalib, who said:
Al-Sufyani will come from the land of the Romans, accepting Christianity (in appearance), with a cross on his neck, and he is the master/leader of the people.

key_terms.السُّفْيَانِيُّ: Al-Sufyani, a specific leader in Shia eschatological narratives
key_terms.بِلَادُ الرُّومِ: The land of the Romans (Byzantine/Eastern Roman Empire regions)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْقَوْمِ: The master or leader of the people/group

ai.seo_question: Who is Al-Sufyani and what are his characteristics before the reappearance of Imam Mahdi?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the Sufyani’s deceptive nature, emerging from Bilad al-Rum (traditionally identified as Syria/Levant) with a cross around his neck to signify his outward Christianity while secretly leading his forces. This duality reflects the Shia eschatological theme of a tyrant who uses religious symbols for political legitimacy before the Mahdi’s appearance. The cross serves as a visual marker of his identity, contrasting with the eventual triumph of the Ahl al-Bayt.
